pages: Foreground: a white wooden cradle on its rockers, dead still, one flat wool blanket inside. Middle: Tam, nine, brown hair cut short, in a rust-red knitted jersey, leaning over the rail with one palm flat on it. Background: the corner of a cold front room, a bare chimney breast. Light: flat grey morning, one long shadow across the floor.

Hob Pike, a broad man of fifty with grizzled hair, stands in the open doorway in his brown oilskin coat, one hand on the frame. Middle distance: the white wooden cradle sitting still in the corner, the bare hearth behind it. Background: the yard wall and the wet lane at mid-morning. Cold grey doorway light on his coat.

Hob Pike, a broad man of fifty with grizzled hair, in his brown oilskin coat, leans one shoulder on the door frame and talks, his hand flat on the jamb. Middle distance: the white wooden cradle on its rails, still as a table. Background: the low beams of Gran's front room, late morning. Cool window light, a thin bar of sun on the boards.

Ruth, thirty-five, brown hair pinned up, in a blue apron over a grey dress, stands at the table with both hands flat on its edge, speaking steadily. Middle distance: the white wooden cradle, still, and a bread board with a cut heel of bread. Background: the front room at dusk, the window gone dark blue. Low lamplight.

Hob Pike, a broad man of fifty with grizzled hair, in a grey waistcoat and rolled shirtsleeves, stands in the middle of Gran's front room with his cap in both hands, saying what is true. Middle distance: the white wooden cradle, motionless on the boards, its shadow still on the wall. Background: the open door and the stair rail, late afternoon. Flat window light.

Tam, nine, brown hair cut short, in a rust-red knitted jersey, stands on the bare kitchen boards looking up, his arms at his sides. Middle distance: the white wooden cradle in the corner and a copper with washing in it by the hearth. Background: the kitchen window and the cold range, morning. Grey window light.

Gran, white hair, a plum shawl over a black dress, stands straight by the cradle rail, one hand on it, answering without raising her voice. Middle distance: the white wooden cradle, still; a folded cloth on the chair beside it. Background: the front room window and the dim corners, a March dusk. Low blue light from the window.

Tam, nine, brown hair cut short, in a rust-red knitted jersey, stands in the dark with his chin lifted, asking a question he has never asked before. Middle distance: the white wooden cradle and the oil lamp on the sill. Background: the open kitchen doorway spilling lamplight, night. One low warm flame, deep cold shadow.

Gran, white hair, a plum shawl over a black dress, takes her hand off the cradle rail and says the true thing out loud. Middle distance: the white wooden cradle beginning to move across the boards, its long shadow swinging on the wall. Background: the front room corner, night, the doorway shut. Low warm lamplight, one moving shadow.

Tam, nine, brown hair cut short, in a rust-red knitted jersey, holds the baby against his shoulder, one hand spread over her back. Middle distance: the white wooden cradle rocking in the corner. Background: the kitchen window at first light, grey and cold, the yard door beyond. Grey dawn light, long shadow on the wall.
